name: Benzene

energies.comment: Atomization energy from gas-phase heat of formation, same method as the other molecules in this dataset: BDE = (6×716.68 + 6×218.0) - 82.9 = 5525.2 kJ/mol. Violation vs naive Kekulé sum (5322) = +203 kJ/mol. CORRECTED from previous value (5470), which was back-computed as naive + 148 (hydrogenation-based resonance energy) rather than measured, making benzene inconsistent with every other entry. See docs/Claude-Reasoning/020.
energies.source: NIST Chemistry WebBook, benzene gas-phase ΔfH° = 82.9 ± 0.9 kJ/mol
energies.source_verification: Value corroborated via secondary search results on 2026-09-30; NIST WebBook and ATcT were not reachable from the verification environment. Primary reference still to be confirmed against the WebBook entry.
energies.hydrogenation_resonance_energy_source: Kistiakowsky et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 1936, 58:146-153 (3×cyclohexene hydrogenation vs benzene hydrogenation)
energies.hydrogenation_resonance_energy_note: Different reference (cyclohexene) than the mean-bond-enthalpy baseline used here; not directly comparable to the violation column.
energies.confidence_note: ΔfH° well established; confidence reduced from 0.95 only because the primary entry was not re-fetched in this pass.

reference_energies.comment: Standard bond energies (kJ/mol) for naive calculation

notes: Bond orders shown as 1.5 to represent delocalized π-system; naive model localizes them into a Kekulé structure (3 C=C, 3 C-C)
Hydrogenation-based resonance energy (cyclohexene reference): ~150 kJ/mol; the two numbers use different baselines
The 203 figure includes mean-bond-enthalpy reference error (hybridization), as do the acyclic polyene values
